name: famistudio-mcp

tools.name: famistudio_info
tools.description: Report whether the FamiStudio executable was found, which version it is, and the paths that were probed. Also lists the CLI export commands this server can run, the directories it is allowed to read and write, WHICH environment variable each of those came from, and whether it fell back to the built-in scratch directory (a sandboxed client often cannot write there).

tools.name: compute_ticks
tools.description: FamiStudio tempo arithmetic. One tick is one frame, so duration is ticks / frameRate (60.0988 NTSC, 50.007 PAL) and the tempo is fixed by the tick grid: bpm = 60 * frameRate / beatLength, i.e. ticks per beat = 60 * frameRate / bpm (~2403 at 150 BPM NTSC). Use it to turn a target duration into a tick count, to see what tempo a tick grid implies, to size a pattern budget, or to check how many notes you can write inside a pattern.

tools.name: analyze_audio
tools.description: Report duration, peak/RMS level and silence for a WAV file, and optionally detect the pitch sequence. Pitch detection expects a monophonic render, e.g. a single channel exported with export_audio + separateChannels.

tools.name: run_famistudio
tools.description: Escape hatch for FamiStudio commands this server does not wrap (NSF export, ROM export, assembly export with exotic options). Runs `FamiStudio <input> <command> <output> [extraArgs...]` with the given argv and no shell involved. Prefer export_audio / export_text when they fit.

command.description: FamiStudio command, e.g. one of: wav-export, mp3-export, ogg-export, nsf-export, rom-export, fds-export, famitracker-txt-export, famistudio-txt-export, famistudio-asm-export, famistudio-asm-sfx-export, famitone2-asm-export, famitone2-asm-sfx-export.

tools.name: compile_song_spec
tools.description:
Compile a compact JSON song specification (channels + notes) into a complete FamiStudio project object, optionally writing it to a .fms file. Object ids, the mandatory instrument envelope masks and the fixed 256-slot pattern tables are filled in automatically. The returned "project" can be passed straight to export_audio / verify_roundtrip / validate_fms. Pass "specPath" instead of "spec" to read the specification from a JSON file. A spec that compiles to zero notes is rejected rather than written as a silent file.

Notes can be written two ways:
  absolute: {"channel":"Square1","notes":[{"time":0,"note":"C4","duration":8},{"time":8,"note":"E4"}]}
  grid:     {"channel":"Square1","notes":["C4",null,null,null,"E4"]}   // one entry per tick
  per pattern: {"channel":"Square1","patterns":[[{"time":0,"note":"C4"}],[{"time":0,"note":"E4"}]]}
In grid form a note without "duration" sustains until the next filled cell; in the "patterns" form
each entry is timed from 0 and becomes one slot in the song sequencer.

Tempo: one tick is ONE FRAME of the console, so seconds = ticks / 60.0988 (NTSC, 50.007 PAL) and
bpm = 60 * frameRate / beatLength. "groove", "noteLength" and "beatLength" do NOT scale that: a
uniform groove of [7] plays exactly as fast as [1]. To get a target tempo, choose the tick grid -
e.g. 4 ticks per beat at 150 BPM means beatLength 24 - or pass "bpm" and let the writer set beatLength.

Notes: use names such as "C4" (FamiStudio spelling, one octave above standard pitch). A NUMBER is a
FamiStudio note value, octave*12 + semitone + 1, so C4 = 49 - it is NOT (octave << 4) | semitone,
where C4 would be 64. Set noteEncoding:"packed" to use that form explicitly.

Limits: patternLength is the cap on ONE pattern (max 256 ticks, FamiStudio notes cannot cross a
pattern boundary); songLength counts patterns (max 256); one channel plays one note per tick, so set
overlapPolicy to "drop" or "shift" for drum parts instead of hitting the default error.

tools.name: validate_fms
tools.description: Check every invariant FamiStudio relies on when loading a project: the mandatory four-envelope instrument masks, the DPCM mapping count, unique object ids, nextUniqueId, reference integrity, note ranges and effect ranges, and the fixed 256-entry pattern tables. Returns the list of problems. Note that "valid" is not the same as "has music": a truncated spec yields a valid, silent project, so an empty project is reported explicitly.

tools.name: read_fms
tools.description: Decode a FamiStudio project file into structured JSON: songs, channels, patterns and notes, plus instrument envelope contents. Set includeNotes=false for a structural overview of large projects. Only version 19 files (FamiStudio 4.5.x) can be read; older files must be re-saved by FamiStudio.

tools.name: summarize_fms
tools.description: Return a readable listing of a project: every song with its pattern order and per-pattern note dumps, plus tick totals and rendered duration. Use this to review what a .fms actually contains.

tools.name: diff_fms
tools.description: Structurally compare two FamiStudio projects (files or inline objects) and list differences in metadata, instruments and per-note content. Use it to confirm that a rewrite did not change the musical content.

tools.name: export_audio
tools.description: Render a FamiStudio project to an audio file with the FamiStudio command line. Requires FamiStudio 4.5.x to be installed; call famistudio_info first if unsure. Returns the artifact path plus duration, peak level and an audibility check for WAV output.

tools.name: export_text
tools.description: Convert a project with `famistudio-txt-export` (FamiStudio text - excellent for verification and for reading note data), `famitracker-txt-export`, or a sound-engine assembly exporter (`famistudio-asm-export`, `famitone2-asm-export`, ...). Returns a preview of the produced file.

tools.name: verify_roundtrip
tools.description: The end-to-end validity check: re-export the project to FamiStudio text and render a WAV, then report whether FamiStudio loaded the file cleanly (no field desync) and produced audio of the expected length. Run this after generating a .fms file.

instructions:
FamiStudio .fms authoring and rendering.

Typical flow: compile_song_spec (or create_fms) -> verify_roundtrip -> export_audio.

Key factual reminders:
- FamiStudio note names are one octave above standard pitch: "C4" sounds ~523 Hz.
- The NES Triangle channel sounds one octave below its note value; keep bass lines low.
- One tick is one frame: seconds = ticks / 60.0988 (NTSC), and the tempo is fixed by the tick
  grid you write - bpm = 60 * frameRate / beatLength. groove/noteLength do NOT scale playback
  speed (a uniform groove of [7] plays exactly as fast as [1]).
- A NUMBER in the spec is a FamiStudio note value, octave*12 + semitone + 1 (C4 = 49). It is not
  (octave << 4) | semitone (C4 = 64); prefer note names such as "C4".
- Limits: patternLength caps ONE pattern at 256 ticks, FamiStudio notes cannot cross a pattern
  boundary, and a channel plays one note per tick (use overlapPolicy for drum parts).
- This writer targets plain 2A03 only (no expansion audio).

Output location - this server does not decide where files go; you do:
- Pass an explicit output path on every writing tool. Absolute paths are used as given.
- Relative paths land in the output directory chosen for this workspace. If none has been
  chosen yet the server asks the user once and remembers the answer for this session only;
  nothing is written to disk to remember it.
- When that happens, record the chosen directory in this workspace's AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md,
  then pass it explicitly on every later call so the server never has to guess.
- Reads are restricted to the configured read roots plus the session output directory, and to
  files this session wrote (so compile -> verify works). To read project files from somewhere
  else, set FAMISTUDIO_MCP_READDIRS; FAMISTUDIO_MCP_OUTDIR sets where output goes, and
  FAMISTUDIO_MCP_WORKSPACE is a one-directory shorthand for both. famistudio_info reports which
  variable each root came from and warns when everything fell back to the built-in temp
  directory - a sandboxed client usually cannot write there.
